Following publication, external complaints regarding several statements in the article were raised through Frontiers' post-publication complaints process. After editorial review of those complaints and the revisions proposed by the author, the article has been corrected as described below.
Corrections have been made to
Introduction
, Paragraph 1.
This sentence previously read as: “Parental alienation (PA) remains one of the most contested concepts in psychiatry, psychology, law, and social work.”
The corrected passage appears below:
“Parental alienation (PA) remains a deeply contested concept in psychiatry, psychology, law, and social work. While the occurrence of alienating behaviors is widely accepted, disagreement spans its validity as a construct, its use in custody adjudication and forensic assessment, and the interpretation of its empirical research base (Bernet, 2020; Harman et al., 2022; Meier, 2020; Kline Pruett et al., 2023).”
This sentence previously read as: “Originally introduced by Gardner (1985) as Parental Alienation Syndrome (PAS), the concept has been excluded from the DSM-5 for insufficient evidence of validity and reliability and removed from the ICD-11 after the World Health Organization determined it ‘is not a health care term' (World Health Organization, 2020).”
The corrected passage appears below:
“Originally introduced by Gardner (1985) as Parental Alienation Syndrome (PAS), the concept has been excluded from the DSM-5, with the vice-chair of the DSM-5 Task Force stating there was ‘not sufficient scientific evidence to warrant its inclusion' (Crary, 2010).
